decisions.rationale: Hypopigmentation is a named, specific pigmentation disorder that the paper treats as a clinical condition in its title and conclusions. It is not one of the excluded general terms.
Prader-Willi syndrome is a single specific genetic disorder with no further categorization, so it is annotated as a Specific Disease using the full phrase as the minimum necessary span.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 Specific Disease; §5 Minimum necessary span

decisions.rationale: This is a duplicate mention of Prader-Willi syndrome in the abstract. Duplicates are annotated separately, and the mention is a standalone noun phrase naming the specific syndrome.
PWS is the abbreviation of Prader-Willi syndrome. Abbreviations are separated into their own mention, so it is annotated as a Specific Disease.
Here hypopigmentation is a standalone noun naming the condition that the criteria define, not a modifier of another noun.
PWS is used as an adjectival modifier of 'individuals' (PWS individuals), so it is annotated as a Modifier rather than as a standalone disease noun.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §3 Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: 'Hypopigmented' is a predicate adjective describing the PWS individuals. Disease mentions used adjectivally, even when not a noun phrase, are annotated as Modifiers.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §3 Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: 'The presence of hypopigmentation' uses hypopigmentation as a standalone noun naming the condition, which is annotated as a Specific Disease.
'The full criteria for hypopigmentation' uses hypopigmentation as a standalone noun naming the condition, so it is a Specific Disease mention.
PWS is used adjectivally to modify 'individuals' (PWS individuals), so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §3 Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: 'With and without hypopigmentation' uses hypopigmentation as a standalone noun naming the condition, not as a modifier, so it is a Specific Disease.
'Hypopigmentation is found in a significant proportion' treats hypopigmentation as a standalone condition noun, so it is a Specific Disease.
'Individuals with PWS' uses PWS as a standalone prepositional object naming the syndrome, not as a compound modifier, so it is annotated as a Specific Disease. This is a judgment call.

decisions.rationale: 'May be associated with a deletion' is preceded by hypopigmentation as a standalone condition noun, so it is a Specific Disease mention.
'The mechanism for the hypopigmentation' uses hypopigmentation as a standalone condition noun, so it is a Specific Disease.
